MP4, WebM ve MKV gibi konteynerler, vide: Containers such as MP4, WebM, and MKV carry video and audio streams in one file. Codecs such as H.264, VP9 or AAC specify the way these streams are encoded.
Bir oynatıcı konteyneri tanıyabilir ama: A player may recognize the container but not support the codec in it. So don't assume every .mp4 file will play on every device.
Video ve ses zaten hedef konteynerle uyu: If video and audio are already compatible with the target container, remux copies the streams without re-encoding. Not recompressing video and audio data prevents loss of quality due to re-encoding.
Remux bir codec’i başka bir codec’e dönü: Remux does not convert one codec to another. There is no guarantee that an unsupported or corrupted stream will be repaired in all cases. ZenithW's remux tool should be used for compatible packaging path.
Bir oynatıcı için farklı bir codec gerek: Conversion may be required when a different codec is required for a player or an audio file with a different encoding such as MP3 is requested from the video. Recoding has an impact on processing time and output quality.
Düşük kaliteli veya kayıplı bir sesi FLA: Converting low quality or lossy audio to FLAC will not restore lost details. It may only increase the file size. ZenithW uses the copy path on appropriate streams, supported re-encoding path when necessary.

Data minimization and account-free use

You do not need to create an account, provide an email address, or build a user profile to use ZenithW. This means identity information that is not required to operate the service is not collected in the first place. We do not create payment or advertising profiles, correlate behavior between users, or sell personal data for advertising.

When you start a job, only the source link, selected format, quality, and relevant processing options are sent to the server. They are used to perform the download, remux, or conversion and to diagnose technical failures.

Links and source platforms

The media link you provide is submitted by the ZenithW server to the source platform to locate the requested content. The source platform and necessary technical providers may process standard network information and the requested URL under their own privacy policies.

ZenithW validates addresses, redirects, and destination IPs to prevent a user-supplied link from reaching internal or local systems. Private, loopback, and link-local network destinations are blocked, and media tools are not allowed to open remote addresses as an independent download path.

Temporary files and protected download links

Media and conversion files created during a job are not a permanent user archive. They remain in temporary storage only long enough to complete the operation and deliver the result, then enter short-lived link and scheduled cleanup workflows. Partial artifacts from expired, failed, or interrupted jobs are also covered by cleanup.

Prepared-file links use hard-to-guess random tokens, expire quickly, are bound to the requesting IP address, and cannot be reused once transfer begins. An active file is protected until its transfer closes, after which interrupted or completed temporary data is removed.

Connection and application security

The web interface and API are delivered over HTTPS. Shared origin verification between the interface and API helps reduce direct unauthorized backend access. Browser security headers restrict framing, content types, referrer exposure, unnecessary device permissions, and the sources from which executable content may load.

File-size, duration, concurrency, temporary-storage, and request-rate limits protect both visitors and service availability. Conversion tools are restricted to local file protocols, while empty, invalid, or over-limit results are rejected rather than delivered as completed files.

IP addresses, security logs, and abuse prevention

Your IP address and limited request details may be processed for rate limiting, concurrency control, prepared-file ownership, attack prevention, troubleshooting, and reliability. These details are used to protect the service, not to build a user profile.

Cloudflare, Amazon Web Services, and other infrastructure providers may create standard connection and security logs. Their contents and retention periods may depend on each provider's operational and security policies; ZenithW uses access to them only when needed to operate and protect the service.

Information that stays in your browser

Download history, language, theme, quality, and filename preferences may be stored in your browser's localStorage. They are not attached to a ZenithW account or synchronized by us across devices. Clearing site data in your browser also removes this local history and these preferences.

The ZenithW application code does not use Google Analytics, advertising pixels, or behavioral-tracking scripts. Browser-stored preferences exist only to personalize the interface and provide local history; they are not used for ad targeting or cross-user profiling.

Your rights, choices, and contact

Because there is no server-side user account, there is no permanent profile record to delete. You may still contact info@zenithw.space with questions about possible processing, correction or deletion requests, or other privacy matters. We request only the information needed to understand and respond to the request.

Contact the source platform first

If the original content is published on a third-party platform, sending a permanent removal request to that platform is usually the most effective route. Still, if you object to a specific source being processed through ZenithW, we can review your notice as well.

  5. A statement that the information is accurate and that you are the rights holder or authorized to act for them.
  6. A physical or electronic signature.

Backend artık Amazon EC2 üzerindeki t3.s: The backend now runs on a t3.small Ubuntu server in Amazon EC2. Gunicorn and gevent preserve the safe single-worker architecture, systemd supervises the app, and Nginx forwards HTTPS and WebSocket traffic. FFmpeg and supporting services run on the same host with explicit resource limits.

Nginx accepts the real visitor IP only through the trusted proxy chain, so rate limits follow the actual user rather than spoofable headers.
Sunucu süreçleri, disk, bellek, ağ ve se: Server processes, disk, memory, networking, and service logs are now directly visible. Nginx, systemd, firewall rules, supporting services, and runtime limits can be tuned for the workload. A dedicated virtual machine is less dependent on an abstract container lifecycle, making diagnostics and performance tuning more measurable.

Operating-system updates, security patches, disk monitoring, service restarts, certificates, and network configuration are now our responsibility. A single EC2 instance is not high availability; there is no automatic second server yet if the host or region has a problem. The server also has a fixed running cost even during quiet periods, and scaling requires more planning than it did on Railway.
ZenithW’nin medya işleme yapısı uzun sür: ZenithW’s media workload relies on long-lived connections, FFmpeg, WebSockets, and controlled temporary storage. For this workload, seeing our Linux host and managing its limits directly became more valuable. We did not move because Railway is bad; we moved because ZenithW now benefits from deeper infrastructure control.
